title: Assignment Expression in an If Condition
explanation: The expression `x = 3` assigns 3 to `x`. An assignment expression evaluates to the assigned value. Since 3 is nonzero, it converts to `true`, so the program prints `A`.

title: Short-Circuit Evaluation Preventing Division by Zero
explanation: `&&` uses short-circuit evaluation. Since `x != 0` is false, the right operand `10 / x > 2` is not evaluated. Therefore division by zero is avoided, and the program prints `B`.

title: Switch Fall-Through Across Multiple Cases
explanation: Execution begins at `case 2`, printing `B`. Because there are no `break` statements, execution continues through `case 3` and then `default`, producing `BCD`, not `BC`.

title: Nested If and Dangling Else
explanation: The first `else` is associated with the nearest unmatched `if`, which is `if (y > 5)`. Since `x > 5` is true and `y > 5` is false, the program prints `B`, not `C`.

title: Chained Relational Comparison
explanation: The expression is parsed as `(1 < x) < 10`. Since `1 < 100` is true, the result behaves numerically as 1. Then `1 < 10` is true, so `Valid` is printed. The intended condition should be `x > 1 && x < 10`.

title: Ternary Operator with Integer Division
explanation: Because `x > y` is true, `x / y` is selected. Both operands are integers, so `5 / 2` performs integer division and produces 2. The value 2 is then converted to `double`, so `result` becomes `2.0`, not `2.5`.

title: Logical OR and Side Effects
explanation: `x == 5` is already true. Because `||` short-circuits when its left operand is true, `++x > 5` is never evaluated. Therefore `x` remains 5.

title: Switch Expression Type Restriction
explanation: A standard C++ `switch` condition must have an integral, enumeration, or suitably convertible class type. A `double` cannot be used directly as the controlling expression, so this code does not compile.

title: Else-If Evaluation Stops After First Match
explanation: An `if`/`else if`/`else` chain selects at most one branch. Since `score >= 90` is true, `A` is printed and the remaining branches are skipped. Although `score >= 80` would also be true if evaluated independently, it is never evaluated here.

title: Nested Ternary Associativity
explanation: The conditional operator is right-associative, so the expression is interpreted as `a > b ? 10 : (b > 5 ? 20 : 30)`. Since `a > b` is false and `b > 5` is true, `result` becomes 20.
